messages:
elaine: Quick sync — drafting the pragmatic sprint for private deploy (VPC/on‑prem) roadmap. Need decisions on: minimal MVP scope, upgrade paths with low downtime, customer-managed networking options (BGP vs relay), and telemetry/telemetry opt-in defaults. Can we lock these before next Monday?

sam: +1. Can we break into three ballot items: 1) MVP installer surface (operator bundle + relay fallback), 2) upgrade choreography (in-place vs blue/green), 3) network modes (customer BGP, NAT, relay). Which is highest risk for launch?

devon: From field: highest-risk is customer BGP. Lots of customers ask for IP preservation & control, but ops teams vary widely. We should treat BGP as "advanced" with clear preflight checks and runbook. Many will accept relay if we provide DNS-preserving cutover.

taylor: Engineering constraints: operator bundle + relay fallback is feasible for MVP. BGP requires an L2/L3 reachability matrix and device templates (Arista/Cisco). For upgrade path, in-place rollout with canary shards is easiest; true zero-downtime blue/green across customer infra is hard. Suggest: default to rolling upgrade with stored backup + automatic rollback, provide blue/green docs for customers that can support it.

elaine: Proposed launch criteria draft: (a) installer completes on a clean host w/ documented preflight in <15 minutes; (b) upgrade test from previous stable in <1hr with automatic rollback; (c) telemetry opt‑in default OFF + clear telemetry keys; (d) fallback relay must serve production traffic for at least one customer in staging. Thoughts?

sam: For (b) we should define what "upgrade test" means programmatically. Dev plan: create small harness that runs a preflight + upgrade + smoke tests. Add a single CLI: `redwoodctl upgrade --dry-run` that returns machine-readable status.

devon: Field asks: add a "customer rollback window" SLA (recommended) — customers expect guidance like "expect 30–60 min maintenance window". Also call out egress IP ownership: some customers need preservation of egress IPs (for ACLs). We'll need a migration pattern for that.

taylor: Notes on egress IP preservation: options are 1) BGP with customer routing (best), 2) NAT with static egress IPs via customer gateway (compromise), 3) relay with preserved source IP via proxy rewrite (hacky). Recommend MVP support NAT + relay; label BGP as enterprise add‑on.

nora: Solutions perspective: offer a "migration package" for early enterprise customers — 2 days of SE time to coordinate BGP handoff. Also propose default telemetry off; allow customers to opt-in with granular controls (errors, perf, anonymized traces). Provide a sample consent CLI: `redwoodctl telemetry enable --errors --perf`

elaine: Agreed on telemetry default OFF. Action items: Sam to spec `redwoodctl` dry-run & telemetry flags, Taylor to draft operator bundle + relay implementation plan, Devon to enumerate customer preflight check matrix (top 10 field customers), Nora to draft enterprise migration package. Target: internal RFC by Thu EOD.

deploy-bot: Ticket created: RDW-PLT-4872 "private-deploy pragmatic sprint RFC" assigned to @elaine, @sam, @taylor, @devon, @nora.

sam: Quick engineering note — add a preflight check for kernel modules + iptables vs nftables and a single line to capture `kubectl` vs non-K8s modes. Example check: ```sh
# preflight snippet
if command -v nft > /dev/null; then echo "nft detected"; fi
```

devon: +1 on checks. Also flag customers on legacy F5 LB configs — can block cutovers. Will add to the matrix.

elaine: Cool. If no objections, I'll book a 30min sync Friday to go over RFC draft. :calendar: :shipit:

sam: ack

taylor: ack

nora: ack :thumbsup:
thread_text_summary: Short coordination thread to lock MVP scope for private deploy roadmap: operator bundle + relay as MVP, BGP as enterprise add-on, rolling upgrade w/ automatic rollback, telemetry default off, action owners assigned
